note: Authored bank for PLUTO vProctor (106 items across all 10 categories, difficulty tiers 1-5). Difficulty tiers seed the Elo b (1000/1150/1300/1450/1600). Every item carries ideal_answer_points, keywords, and a scoring_rubric for the Tier-1/Tier-2 graders. Recommend SME review (correctness, de-biased HR content) before any production use.

questions.text: What is the difference between a hash map and a balanced binary search tree? When would you choose each?
ideal_answer_points: Hash map: average O(1) lookup/insert, unordered
BST: O(log n) operations, keeps keys ordered
Hash map has worst-case O(n) on collisions; no ordered traversal
Choose BST when range queries / ordering / sorted iteration are needed
Choose hash map for fast point lookups with no ordering need

questions.text: Explain how a deadlock can occur between two threads and describe two distinct strategies to prevent it.
ideal_answer_points: Deadlock arises when threads hold locks and wait on each other cyclically

Prevention 1: consistent global lock ordering to break circular wait
Prevention 2: lock timeouts / try-lock with backoff, or avoiding hold-and-wait
Trade-offs of each strategy

questions.text: What does it mean for a REST API to be idempotent? Which HTTP methods should be idempotent and why does it matter?
ideal_answer_points: Idempotent = repeating the same request yields the same server state
GET, PUT, DELETE, HEAD are idempotent; POST generally is not
Why it matters: safe retries on network failure without duplicates
Idempotency keys as a technique for making POST safe to retry

questions.text: A read-heavy service backed by a single SQL database is hitting latency limits under load. Walk me through how you would diagnose and scale it.
ideal_answer_points: Measure first: identify slow queries, indexes, and the real bottleneck

Introduce caching (application cache / Redis) for hot reads
Add read replicas and route reads to them

questions.text: What does a load balancer do, and what are a couple of strategies it can use to distribute traffic?

questions.text: Explain the difference between database replication and sharding, and what each solves.
ideal_answer_points: Replication copies data across nodes

Sharding partitions data across nodes by a key
Improves write scaling and storage capacity
Trade-offs: replication lag; cross-shard queries

Fan-out on read: assemble the feed at request time
